incidents.vector: Apparent long-running breach of a widely used identity verification provider, with ID scans continuously exfiltrated for over a year and sold via a new dark web service called Nexus.
incidents.impact: More than 153 million US and Canadian driver's license scans, plus millions of other ID documents, are for sale on a Russian cybercrime forum; records include senior US government officials. The FBI has opened an inquiry and the dataset is still growing daily.

incidents.vector: Compromise of Cisco IOS XR routers, TACACS authentication servers, and management infrastructure using custom router malware, credential harvesting, and log tampering.
incidents.impact: Attackers used compromised routers as vantage points to capture network traffic, harvest administrator credentials, and pivot into connected high-value and critical infrastructure environments. Activity continued into 2026 with victims and third parties affected.

incidents.vector: ClickFix social engineering via compromised websites and fake Cloudflare verification overlays, with a backdoor that retrieves its command-and-control address from the Polygon blockchain (EtherHiding).
incidents.impact: At least 31 organizations compromised with a persistent backdoor that beacons every minute and cannot be severed by blocking a single domain; assessed as initial access brokering that could enable follow-on ransomware.

incidents.victim: Aviation, aerospace and fintech developers (Egypt, Ethiopia, Afghanistan)
incidents.vector: Fake recruiters on LinkedIn and job platforms delivered malicious coding assignments hiding two new malware families (remote access trojans) under time pressure to prevent scrutiny.
incidents.impact: Developers' Windows, Linux and macOS systems infected with previously undocumented remote-access malware, giving persistent access to machines of technology specialists in sensitive industries across Africa and the Middle East.

incidents.vector: Unauthorized access to information systems of a subsidiary, detected in mid-August 2026; method not disclosed.
incidents.impact: Exposed internal patient ID numbers for over 1,400 US patient records, identifying data for fewer than 50 patients, and contact details for providers and employees. Medical treatment devices were not accessed and operations are unaffected.

incidents.vector: OAuth consent phishing over a commercial messaging app: attackers impersonate officials and journalists and trick targets into authorizing a malicious cloud application, bypassing passwords and MFA.
incidents.impact: Victims unknowingly grant attackers persistent, token-based access to email, files and other sensitive cloud data; access survives password changes. FBI issued a public alert on the campaign, active since late 2025.

incidents.vector: Exploitation of CVE-2026-82329, a critical (CVSS 9.8) authentication bypass in default Artifactory configurations, beginning three days after disclosure; public proof-of-concept now available.
incidents.impact: Multiple threat actors are minting admin tokens and enumerating users, credentials and federated access on exposed instances. Admin access to a central artifact repository enables software supply chain tampering; exposed systems should be treated as compromised.

incidents.vector: Intrusion into company servers with exfiltration of patient, employee, provider and financial data; extortion demand with threat to publish.
incidents.impact: Operator of 27 hospitals and outpatient facilities in 12 states is being extorted by a Russia-based ransomware-as-a-service group that claimed the attack on its leak site; a class action has already been filed. Scope of stolen data still under investigation.

incidents.vector: ClickFix-style fake CAPTCHA overlays trick users into pasting a malicious command into PowerShell, leading to DLL sideloading, payloads hidden in PNG images, and a Python-based reverse tunnel into internal networks.
incidents.impact: Attackers gain persistent, direct access to victims' internal networks, typically followed by privilege escalation, disabling of security controls, data exfiltration and ransomware deployment, per Microsoft.

incidents.vector: Not yet disclosed; hackers breached user accounts and accessed data.
incidents.impact: Bloomberg reported that Dropbox user accounts were breached and data accessed; scope and attacker not yet public.

incidents.victim: Sality botnet victims (15,000+ infected machines worldwide)
incidents.vector: 20-year-old polymorphic file-infecting malware forming a peer-to-peer botnet, monetized mainly via clipboard hijacking that swapped cryptocurrency wallet addresses.
incidents.impact: CrowdStrike, DOJ, FBI and European partners sinkholed the botnet on Aug 31, severing the operator's control of 15,000+ machines that had been used for crypto theft (est. $150K+ stolen) and occasional DDoS attacks. Infected hosts now beacon to defender-run sinkholes for victim notification.

incidents.vector: Voice phishing via external Microsoft Teams accounts posing as IT help desks, coercing employees into running remote-access tools or custom malware; one variant escalated to an NTLM relay attack against domain controllers.
incidents.impact: Coordinated vishing operation (Jan-Apr 2026) targeted more than 150 employees at 10+ organizations, attempting to establish footholds and domain-level access via legitimate remote management software.

incidents.vector: Large-scale distributed denial-of-service attack against Digdir, the IT provider for Norwegian government portals.
incidents.impact: Users were unable to log into Norwegian government portals for several hours; a pro-Kremlin hacktivist group claimed responsibility citing Norway's support for Ukraine.

incidents.vector: Compromise of a third-party application, likely via social engineering or identity weaknesses in cloud-hosted environments, with a four-day data exfiltration window (Aug 21-25).
incidents.impact: Data stolen from oncology, multispecialty and medical-surgical business units of the distributor of roughly one-third of North American pharmaceuticals, with intermittent service degradation. Extortionists reportedly demanded over $55 million; McKesson says attackers are no longer in its systems.

incidents.vector: Network intrusion into two Berlin ministries (urban development and transport) with data theft between Aug 7-12, followed by an extortion demand.
incidents.impact: Attackers claim 5.79 TB of government data including contracts, emails, passwords and classified material, auctioned for ~$2.3M after Berlin refused to pay. Two ministries were cut off from the state network, disrupting email, internet and some citizen services weeks before Berlin's Sept 20 elections.

incidents.victim: US Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF)
incidents.vector: Breach of a standalone ATF system by a ransomware group; entry method not disclosed.
incidents.impact: The compromised system contained information on ATF investigation targets. The agency says only one standalone system was accessed and its main network and public portals were unaffected.

incidents.vector: Data theft from systems holding traveler information, including WiFi sign-up records, followed by a ransom demand which the company refused.
incidents.impact: Data of 8.7 million travelers who passed through Manchester, East Midlands and London Stansted airports was stolen, including email addresses used for airport WiFi registration.

incidents.vector: Cyberattack on systems used to process and ship customer orders; method not disclosed.
incidents.impact: Global operations of the ~60,000-employee medical device maker were disrupted, affecting order processing and shipping. Disclosed to the SEC.

incidents.victim: Philippine Nuclear Research Institute and naval contractor
incidents.vector: Network intrusions into the Philippine nuclear agency and a major naval contractor; details limited.
incidents.impact: Suspected Chinese state-backed hackers breached sensitive Philippine government and defense-industrial organizations amid regional tensions.

incidents.vector: Data theft followed by a $3.3 million ransom demand; data published after the company refused to pay.
incidents.impact: Records of almost 13 million customers leaked online, though the dataset also contained millions of synthetic fake records.

incidents.victim: European government and diplomatic organizations (Romania, Spain, Türkiye)
incidents.vector: Spearphishing with macro-enabled Word documents using diplomatic lures, deploying a lightweight batch-script backdoor that abuses legitimate webhook services for command-and-control and exfiltration.
incidents.impact: Sustained initial-access campaigns (Sept 2025 - April 2026) against defense and diplomatic targets, including lures tied to Spanish-Moldovan meetings ahead of Moldova's elections; higher-value victims received a faster-beaconing second-stage implant.

incidents.victim: Open-source software ecosystem (TeamPCP supply chain attacks)
incidents.vector: Self-propagating worm embedded in compromised open-source libraries stole developer credentials and re-injected itself into other packages, compromising projects like Trivy, KICS, LiteLLM and Telnyx.
incidents.impact: Australian police arrested two alleged members, including the suspected leader, of the group behind the longest-running software supply chain attack spree, which harvested 500,000+ credentials and led to ransomware and extortion at major companies and government bodies.

incidents.victim: US critical infrastructure PLC operators (Siemens S7 series)
incidents.vector: Internet scanning for exposed Siemens S7 PLCs, then AI-generated exploitation scripts disguised as legitimate monitoring tools abusing open-source industrial libraries for read/write access to controllers.
incidents.impact: NSA, CISA, FBI, DOE and EPA warn of active reconnaissance and capability development against US PLC installations across manufacturing, energy, water, chemical and food sectors, assessed as pre-positioning for future operational disruption.
